entries.title: Summary starts writing itself when you open it
entries.body: Pressing Summary on one of your articles that has no summary yet starts writing one, instead of leaving an empty panel, and the panel no longer says nobody has asked while one is being written. Summary is also among the main modes you can choose to have prepared when you add an article.

entries.title: Archive button at the top of the article
entries.body: On your own articles, an Archive button sits at the top of the reading page beside the sharing mark, and Put back undoes it. It stays in step with the same control on the article's Metadata page.

entries.title: Your plan and any gifts are explained
entries.body: Your profile page and the allowance box in your library show your plan, any gifts you received, and how it works, such as when limits reset. If someone gives you a gift and you have an account, the email can show your allowance before and after it, and may carry a note from the giver. The privacy policy says so.

entries.title: Experimental: the margin gathers notes from other modes
entries.body: With the Experimental features switch on your profile page, the Marginalia column to the right of the article also shows FAQ answers, Debate sources, citations and your comments, one line each beside the passage they belong to, opening in place. Opening the column starts no new AI work.

entries.title: Experimental: a new typeface for the AI's words
entries.body: With the Experimental features switch on your profile page, text the AI wrote appears in IBM Plex Mono instead of Courier Prime. The author's words, the AI's and your own each keep their own typeface in more places, including Tweets, Quotes, Sketch, hover cards, chat and search, while the app's own labels stay in its usual type.

entries.title: More Dig deeper presses each day in Citations
entries.body: The daily limit on Dig deeper in Citations, shared by all readers together, went from 25 to 62. Your own limit of 20 a day is unchanged, so you should meet the daily-limit message less often on a busy day.

entries.title: The reading page no longer scrolls sideways
entries.body: On a Mac set to always show scrollbars, every article could scroll a little sideways, because the page counted the scrollbar as room to fill. It fits the window now. On very wide windows, the panel beside the article also uses the spare room.

entries.title: Metadata page contents list shows on an iPad
entries.body: The contents list in the left margin of an article's Metadata page was hidden on medium-width windows, such as an iPad held sideways. It shows there now, and the page moves over just enough to make room for it.
